rows.sos_note: Faced BUF (31st), KC (3rd), LV (28th), MIA (27th), NE (14th) (run defense rank). Those defenses allowed 2% more yards per carry to RBs than average, so recent games adjust to 69.1 (raw 73.5).
rows.why: Check the news first — we expect 60.2 but the line is 33.5. A gap this big usually means the sportsbook knows something (a role change, an injury). No bet: we expect about 60.2 rushing yards vs the 33.5 line — not enough to clear the price (needs 56% per pick on Underdog)
rows.why_long: Underdog higher 33.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 50% (median line). Averaging 73.5 over the last 8 games, higher than 33.5 in 76% of them (raw 79%, shrunk 56%). LAC allows -5% to RBs → projects 60.2 (raw 73%, shrunk 55%).
why_points: The pick: Rush yds higher 33.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the app sets its lines as medians, so with no sportsbook listing this player the fair view is 50%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 33.5. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 40, 33, 147, 104, 78, 116, 59, 14. Weighted average 73.5; went higher than 33.5 in 6 of 8 games (76% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±43.1, so the line is 0.9 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Matchup: LAC has allowed -5% vs the league average to RBs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -4% on his average.
PFF: LAC plays man on 23% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 27%); he gains 0.87 yds/route vs man and 1.02 vs zone → +1% from scheme.
PFF: LAC allows 1.14 yds/route to RBs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.29) → -11% against his usual opponents.
PFF: NYJ's run blocking vs LAC's run defense: 1.1 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 1.3, league 1.1); he adds 3.4 after contact → -4% per carry.
Projection: we expect 60.2 rushing yards on average; in a typical game 53.9 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 20.4 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 79% and the matchup 73%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 56%, matchup 55%.
Bottom line: we give it 55% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: -0.5 points; that works out to about -1¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: Pass: the line looks about right (we expect about 53.9 in a typical game vs the 33.5 line).
